lessons.title: Meet the kit
lessons.summary: Learn the core voices, balanced setup, and safe listening habits.

lessons.title: Count the grid
lessons.summary: Read quarter and eighth notes as positions in time.

lessons.title: Build your first backbeat
lessons.summary: Coordinate kick, snare, and hi-hat into a full groove.

lessons.title: A fill that lands
lessons.summary: Move singles around the kit and return cleanly to beat one.

lessons.title: Sixteenth-note control
lessons.summary: Subdivide one beat into four equally spaced notes.

lessons.title: Orchestrate the paradiddle
lessons.summary: Turn sticking into musical movement between snare and toms.

lessons.title: Own the offbeat
lessons.summary: Add syncopated kick notes without disturbing the snare.

lessons.title: Linear fill design
lessons.summary: Build fills where no two limbs strike together.

lessons.title: Layer independence
lessons.summary: Hold a foot ostinato while your hands phrase above it.
goals: Add one hand at a time

lessons.title: Make five feel natural
lessons.summary: Group 5/4 as 3 + 2 and create a repeatable pocket.

lessons.title: Shape a dynamic arc
lessons.summary: Control ghost notes, accents, and crescendos without changing tempo.

meet-the-kit.idea: A drum kit is a group of distinct voices. A relaxed setup lets each limb reach its instrument without twisting or lifting the shoulders.
steps: Name kick, snare, hi-hat, tom, and crash. On the Practice Pad, those voices use Space, F, J, K, and L.
Sit so your thighs slope slightly down and your feet can rest on the pedals without reaching.
Use hearing protection around acoustic drums and keep headphone or monitor levels comfortable.

count-the-grid.idea: A steady beat is a set of evenly spaced positions. Eighth notes split each beat into two equal spaces.
steps: Say “1 & 2 & 3 & 4 &” at a comfortable pace. The numbers are the beats; each “&” sits halfway between them.
Watch the Practice Pad playhead move through the numbered grid.
Tap the snare evenly on every eighth-note position, then repeat while counting aloud.

first-backbeat.idea: A common rock and pop groove pairs kick on beats 1 and 3 with snare on beats 2 and 4. Even hi-hat eighths connect the pattern.
steps: Count “1 & 2 & 3 & 4 &” before playing.
Add the hi-hat on each number and “&”. Keep its volume even.
Add kick on 1 and 3, then snare on 2 and 4. Keep the count moving through the whole bar.

first-fill.idea: A fill adds a short phrase near the end of a groove. A clear downbeat after the fill makes the transition feel settled.
steps: Play a simple groove for three beats and keep counting through beat 4.
Use even eighth notes across the snare and tom on beat 4.
Land kick and crash together on the next beat 1. Start slowly enough to make that landing comfortable.

sixteenth-control.idea: Sixteenth notes divide a beat into four equal positions, commonly counted “1 e & a”. Relaxed, even spacing matters more than speed.
steps: Say “1 e & a” several times without playing.
Play four quiet, even snare taps on each beat.
Keep your hands low and relaxed. Increase tempo only while every subdivision stays even.

paradiddle-voices.idea: A single paradiddle is R-L-R-R, L-R-L-L. The repeated strokes are doubles; accents can make the sticking easier to hear.
steps: Say the sticking out loud and make the repeated hand change feel smooth.
Accent the first note of each four-note group while keeping the other notes lower.
Move selected notes from snare to tom without changing the sticking or pulse.

syncopated-pocket.idea: Syncopation places a note between the main beats. Keep the snare backbeat steady while the kick adds offbeat movement.
steps: Count the eighth-note grid and keep snare on beats 2 and 4.
Add one kick on an “&” while keeping the other notes unchanged.
Repeat the bar and notice whether the offbeat kick pulls the next beat early.

linear-fill.idea: A linear phrase gives each subdivision to one voice at a time. Separating the voices makes a fill clear and controlled.
steps: Count each subdivision at a slow tempo.
Play the kick, snare, and tom sequence one note at a time; let each sound finish before the next voice.
Keep the final subdivision clear so the next groove can begin on beat 1.

limb-independence.idea: Independence grows by layering one steady part at a time. Make the foot pattern automatic before adding a hand part.
steps: Tap a steady kick pulse and count aloud for several bars.
Keep the kick going while adding a simple hi-hat pulse.
Add the snare backbeat last. If a layer slips, remove it and rebuild from the pulse.

five-four.idea: Five-four has five quarter-note beats in each bar. Grouping it as 3 + 2 gives the phrase a repeatable shape.
steps: Count “1 2 3, 1 2” and accent each group’s first beat.
Keep the hi-hat evenly spaced across all five beats.
Place the kick and snare while keeping the 3 + 2 count audible.

dynamic-arc.idea: Dynamics describe how softly or strongly you play. A quiet note and an accent should differ in volume while staying in time.
steps: Play one bar of soft notes at an easy tempo.
Repeat with one clear accent, keeping the remaining notes soft.
Build the volume gradually over four bars without speeding up.

three-over-two.idea: A 3:2 polyrhythm places three evenly spaced notes over the same span as two evenly spaced notes. Learn each pulse separately before combining them.
steps: Clap two even notes across a steady two-beat span.
Over the same span, sing three evenly spaced notes: “1, trip, let”.
Keep the two-beat pulse in your foot while speaking the three-note phrase. Begin slowly.

rudiments.name: Single Stroke Roll
rudiments.coaching: Let the stick rebound; match the height of both hands.
rudiments.description: Even alternating hands, the foundation of speed and control.

rudiments.name: Double Stroke Roll
rudiments.coaching: Make the second stroke rebound, not squeeze.
rudiments.description: Two controlled strokes per hand with consistent spacing.

rudiments.name: Single Paradiddle
rudiments.sticking: R L R R  L R L L
rudiments.coaching: Accent the first note of each four-note group.
rudiments.description: Alternating singles and doubles that unlock orchestration.

rudiments.name: Six Stroke Roll
rudiments.sticking: R L L R R L
rudiments.coaching: Keep the doubles low and the outside singles relaxed.
rudiments.description: A flowing six-note phrase for fills and solos.

rudiments.name: Flam Control
rudiments.coaching: Keep the grace note low and close to the main stroke.
rudiments.description: Four evenly spaced flams; the grace note should lead each main stroke without becoming a double stroke.

rudiments.name: Single Drag Taps
rudiments.coaching: Keep both grace notes quiet and resolve them into one clear tap.
rudiments.description: A measured drag before each main note, with the final tap aligned to the pulse.

rudiments.name: Buzz Roll Control
rudiments.coaching: Use relaxed pressure and let the buzz sustain evenly.
rudiments.description: Four controlled buzz strokes leading into the pulse, paced slowly for clarity.

grooves.name: Quarter Note Pulse
grooves.focus: Keep an even pulse while placing kick and snare
grooves.description: Start with one hi-hat note per beat, kick on 1 and 3, and snare on 2 and 4.

grooves.name: First Backbeat
grooves.focus: Steady eighth notes and a strong backbeat
grooves.description: Your first complete beat: hats on eighths, kick on 1 and 3, snare on 2 and 4.

grooves.name: Straight Pop Beat
grooves.focus: Keep the eighth-note hat even and the backbeat clear
grooves.description: A steady pop foundation with a consistent kick, snare, and closed hi-hat pattern.

grooves.name: Two Beat Rock
grooves.focus: Hear a strong snare on beats 2 and 4
grooves.description: A stripped-down rock groove that leaves room to focus on the backbeat.

grooves.name: Four on the Floor
grooves.focus: Keep four steady kick notes under the backbeat
grooves.description: Kick every beat, snare on 2 and 4, and even eighth-note hi-hat.

grooves.name: Half Time Rock
grooves.focus: Leave space and place the snare on beat 3
grooves.description: The pulse stays steady while the snare lands once per bar on beat 3.

grooves.name: Punk Drive
grooves.focus: Keep the eighth notes even at a brisk tempo
grooves.description: A fast, straight eighth-note groove with a firm kick and backbeat.

grooves.name: Disco Offbeat Hat
grooves.focus: Lift the offbeat hi-hat without rushing the kick
grooves.description: Four-on-the-floor kick with a lifted offbeat hat accent and steady backbeat.

grooves.name: Motown Pocket
grooves.focus: Make the kick and backbeat feel relaxed and consistent
grooves.description: A warm eighth-note pocket with a small kick pickup into beat 3.

grooves.name: Reggae One Drop
grooves.focus: Leave beat 1 open and land the band hit on beat 3
grooves.description: Kick and snare meet on beat 3 while the hi-hat carries the pulse.

grooves.name: Reggae Steppers
grooves.focus: Keep an even quarter-note kick beneath the hat
grooves.description: A steady kick on every beat with a light backbeat on 2 and 4.

grooves.name: Ska Upbeat
grooves.focus: Place the snare on the offbeat eighth notes
grooves.description: A brisk upbeat pattern with snare on the '&' counts and kick on the quarter pulse.

grooves.name: Country Train Beat
grooves.focus: Alternate kick and snare evenly under the hats
grooves.description: A driving train-like pattern with an alternating low and backbeat voice.

grooves.name: Blues Shuffle
grooves.focus: Keep the long-short triplet feel relaxed
grooves.description: A swung triplet-grid shuffle with kick on 1 and 3 and snare on 2 and 4.

grooves.name: Jazz Swing Ride Pattern
grooves.focus: Ride the triplet pulse and keep the feathered kick quiet
grooves.description: A basic swung ride pattern with a light hi-hat on beats 2 and 4. Use the hi-hat voice as your ride cymbal guide.

grooves.name: Bossa Nova
grooves.focus: Keep the cross-stick backbeat while the kick syncopates
grooves.description: An original bossa-inspired coordination study with a syncopated kick and steady eighth-note guide.

grooves.name: Samba Drive
grooves.focus: Coordinate the repeating kick figure against the backbeat
grooves.description: A brisk, original samba-inspired kit exercise with repeated bass drum notes.

grooves.name: Syncopated Funk Pocket
grooves.focus: Place offbeat kicks without disturbing the backbeat
grooves.description: Anchor the snare while the kick moves between the pulse; keep sixteenth-note subdivisions clear.

grooves.name: Broken Beat
grooves.focus: Count the sixteenths while the accents shift around the bar
grooves.description: A syncopated study in displaced kick and snare accents over a steady subdivision.

grooves.name: Five-Four Drive
grooves.focus: Feel five as 3 + 2
grooves.description: A musical five-beat groove with a clear grouping.

grooves.name: Seven-Eight Grouping
grooves.focus: Group the seven eighth notes as 2 + 2 + 3
grooves.description: A short odd-meter phrase with a clear kick grouping and a snare anchor near the end.

grooves.name: Five-Four Half Time
grooves.focus: Hold the five-beat phrase while leaving space around the snare
grooves.description: An open five-beat groove with a half-time backbeat and a steady eighth-note guide.

grooves.name: Sparse Rock Backbeat
grooves.focus: Keep the backbeat steady while leaving the kick space
grooves.description: A relaxed eighth-note hat line with only one kick and a clear two-and-four snare.

grooves.name: Quarter Kick Backbeat
grooves.focus: Keep the kick even under a steady backbeat
grooves.description: Quarter-note kicks support the familiar snare on beats two and four.

grooves.name: Slow Rock Drive
grooves.focus: Stay relaxed through a slow eighth-note pattern
grooves.description: A slow, open rock beat that helps build even hands and dependable snare placement.

grooves.name: Kick Pickup Intro
grooves.focus: Place a simple pickup without rushing the next bar
grooves.description: Add one extra kick on the final offbeat while the hi-hat and backbeat stay steady.

grooves.name: Tom Pulse
grooves.focus: Move between tom and snare while keeping the pulse
grooves.description: A simple alternating tom and snare exercise with an eighth-note guide.

grooves.name: Three-Quarter Waltz
grooves.focus: Feel the first beat of each three-beat bar
grooves.description: A simple waltz pulse with kick on one, snare on two, and a light final beat.

grooves.name: First Six-Eight Pulse
grooves.focus: Count six even eighth notes in two groups of three
grooves.description: A basic compound-meter exercise with kick on the first pulse and snare on the fourth.

grooves.name: Quarter-Note Backbeat
grooves.focus: Keep quarter notes even and put the snare on two and four
grooves.description: A sparse pattern with one note per beat across the hi-hat, kick, and snare.

grooves.name: Hat Accent Alternation
grooves.focus: Alternate strong downbeats with quieter offbeats
grooves.description: Play eight steady hi-hat notes and make the main beats stand out from the offbeats.

grooves.name: Crash and Land
grooves.focus: Coordinate a crash with the first kick
grooves.description: Start the bar with a crash and kick together, then settle into a simple backbeat.

grooves.name: Four Even Kicks
grooves.focus: Keep the bass drum even on every beat
grooves.description: Four quarter-note kicks create a stable base under the two-and-four backbeat.

grooves.name: Rock Kick Pickup
grooves.focus: Place the kick pickup on the final eighth note
grooves.description: A familiar backbeat with a kick pickup that pulls the phrase into the next bar.

grooves.name: Rock Offbeat Kick
grooves.focus: Keep an offbeat kick from pulling the snare forward
grooves.description: Shift one bass drum note to the '&' after beat two while the snare anchors two and four.

grooves.name: Indie Open Space
grooves.focus: Hold time through a bar with fewer kick notes
grooves.description: The hats and backbeat keep moving while the kick leaves room between its two notes.

grooves.name: Sixteenth R&B Pocket
grooves.focus: Count sixteenth notes while keeping the snare settled
grooves.description: A lightly syncopated kick and snare pattern over a full sixteenth-note hat guide.

grooves.name: Ghost Note Pocket
grooves.focus: Separate quiet snare taps from backbeat accents
grooves.description: Keep the main backbeat strong and place softer snare notes around it.

grooves.name: Sixteenth Disco Drive
grooves.focus: Keep the kick on each beat while the hand subdivides
grooves.description: Four-on-the-floor kick under a continuous sixteenth-note hat pattern and steady snare.

grooves.name: Classic Shuffle Pocket
grooves.focus: Keep the skipped triplet note light
grooves.description: A swung triplet hat line with kick on one and three and snare on two and four.

grooves.name: Walking Shuffle Kick
grooves.focus: Maintain the shuffle while the kick walks through the bar
grooves.description: A triplet shuffle with an extra kick note leading into the second half of the measure.

grooves.name: Ride and Comp
grooves.focus: Keep the ride flowing while placing snare comp notes
grooves.description: A ride-like triplet guide with sparse snare comping and a light hi-hat on two and four.

grooves.name: Ska Two-Step
grooves.focus: Keep the upbeat snares light and even
grooves.description: A brisk two-and-four kick with snare notes on the eighth-note upbeats.

grooves.name: Reggae Rockers
grooves.focus: Keep the kick on each beat with a relaxed backbeat
grooves.description: A steady roots-style kit exercise with four kicks and a light snare on two and four.

grooves.name: Afrobeat Interlock
grooves.focus: Coordinate a repeating kick figure under even hats
grooves.description: A repeating syncopated kick line and sparse snare pattern make a coordination study.

grooves.name: Soul Hat Lift
grooves.focus: Lift selected hat notes without changing the backbeat
grooves.description: A steady soul groove with selected offbeat hi-hat accents and a moving kick pickup.

grooves.name: Three-Quarter Rock
grooves.focus: Place the backbeat on beat three of a waltz bar
grooves.description: A rock pattern in three with a kick on one and a snare on three.

grooves.name: Six-Eight Blues
grooves.focus: Group the six pulses into two groups of three
grooves.description: A compound-time shuffle with a bass drum on the first pulse and snare on the fourth.

grooves.name: Four-on-the-Floor Hat Lift
grooves.focus: Keep every kick solid as the hat accents move
grooves.description: A four-kick dance pattern with a lifted offbeat hat accent and a stable snare.

grooves.name: Straight Sixteenth Rock
grooves.focus: Keep the sixteenth-note hand motion even
grooves.description: A straight rock backbeat beneath a full sixteenth-note hi-hat guide.

grooves.name: Cascara-Inspired Study
grooves.focus: Keep the repeating bell-like hand pattern even
grooves.description: An original coordination study with a repeating accented hand pattern and syncopated kick.

grooves.name: Linear Funk Basics
grooves.focus: Keep kick, snare, and hat strokes from colliding
grooves.description: A linear sixteenth-note phrase that moves between voices while maintaining the pulse.

grooves.name: Double-Kick Metal Grid
grooves.focus: Keep fast bass drum notes even beneath the backbeat
grooves.description: A demanding sixteenth-note kick ostinato with a steady snare and eighth-note hand guide.

grooves.name: Drum and Bass Half-Time
grooves.focus: Feel the half-time snare against a quick subdivision
grooves.description: A brisk sixteenth-note guide with a spacious snare on beat three and syncopated kick.

grooves.name: Gospel Sixteenth Pocket
grooves.focus: Fit displaced snare accents around the anchor beats
grooves.description: A busy sixteenth-note coordination pattern with syncopated kick and snare accents.

grooves.name: Second-Line Study
grooves.focus: Maintain a buoyant pulse through syncopated accents
grooves.description: An original parade-style coordination exercise with displaced snare and kick accents.

grooves.name: Clave Coordination Study
grooves.focus: Keep a two-bar accent phrase steady across the bar line
grooves.description: A two-bar-inspired, original kit coordination pattern with shifting accents and open space.

grooves.name: Six-Eight Rock Drive
grooves.focus: Drive two groups of three without flattening the meter
grooves.description: A strong compound rock pulse with bass drum on one and four and snare on four.

grooves.name: Twelve-Eight Slow Shuffle
grooves.focus: Hold four triplet groups with a deep backbeat
grooves.description: A spacious triplet-grid groove with a rolling ride guide and backbeat on beats two and four.

grooves.name: Nine-Eight Grouping
grooves.focus: Hear the final group of three before the bar turns
grooves.description: An odd-meter exercise with nine eighth-note steps grouped as two, two, two, and three.

grooves.name: Seven-Eight 3 + 2 + 2
grooves.focus: Keep the three-note opening group distinct
grooves.description: A seven-eighth phrase grouped as three, two, and two with clear kick and snare anchors.

grooves.name: Five-Four 2 + 3
grooves.focus: Feel the two-beat pickup into the longer group
grooves.description: A five-beat rock phrase grouped as two plus three with a stable eighth-note guide.

grooves.name: Five-Four Syncopation
grooves.focus: Keep syncopated kicks inside the five-beat phrase
grooves.description: A more displaced kick pattern over a five-beat grouping, with snare notes marking the turns.

grooves.name: Jazz Waltz Ride
grooves.focus: Keep the triplet ride flowing across three beats
grooves.description: A triplet-grid ride pattern with light kick support and sparse snare comping.

grooves.name: Twelve-Eight Gospel Pulse
grooves.focus: Keep a flowing triplet hand while displacing the kick
grooves.description: A compound triplet exercise with a steady guide, moving kick, and backbeat anchors.

grooves.name: Broken Sixteenth Hats
grooves.focus: Keep a consistent internal sixteenth-note count
grooves.description: A broken hat orchestration with gaps while syncopated kit voices fill the rhythmic space.

grooves.name: Four-Beat Accent Displacement
grooves.focus: Hold the backbeat while accents shift every three steps
grooves.description: A repeating accent cycle crosses the bar line over a stable four-beat foundation.

grooves.name: One-Bar Tom Ascent
grooves.focus: Move a steady sixteenth-note fill around the kit
grooves.description: A one-bar fill study that moves from snare to toms and lands on a crash.

grooves.name: One-Bar Tom Descent
grooves.focus: Play even singles while moving down the toms
grooves.description: A descending fill that travels from high tom back to snare with a clear final accent.

grooves.name: One-Bar Linear Fill
grooves.focus: Play the fill without overlapping drum voices
grooves.description: A challenging linear fill where each sixteenth-note step moves to a different kit voice.

grooves.name: Rock Groove → Fill
grooves.focus: Keep the first bar steady and make the second-bar fill resolve
grooves.description: Play a straight rock beat for one bar, then move through a simple snare and tom fill. The phrase loops back to the downbeat.

grooves.name: Pop Groove → Fill
grooves.focus: Keep the pop backbeat clear before a compact fill
grooves.description: A steady pop bar followed by a short tom fill and a crash to lead into the next loop.

grooves.name: Funk Groove → Fill
grooves.focus: Preserve the syncopated pocket through the fill
grooves.description: A syncopated sixteenth-note funk bar moves into a linear fill that resolves with a crash.

grooves.name: Shuffle → Triplet Fill
grooves.focus: Keep the swung subdivision consistent into the fill
grooves.description: A blues shuffle bar followed by a triplet-based snare and tom fill with a clear resolution.

grooves.name: Half-Time Groove → Fill
grooves.focus: Hold the slow backbeat while counting the faster fill
grooves.description: A spacious half-time first bar contrasts with a sixteenth-note fill in the second bar.

grooves.name: Fill: Quarter-Note Snare
grooves.focus: Keep four evenly spaced strokes across the bar
grooves.description: A first fill using one relaxed snare hit on each beat. Count 1, 2, 3, 4 and leave the spaces even.

grooves.name: Fill: Eighth-Note Snare
grooves.focus: Keep the eighth-note hand motion steady
grooves.description: Play two snare notes per beat with an even, unaccented touch before adding speed.

grooves.name: Fill: Beat Four Eighths
grooves.focus: Start the fill on beat four and land the next downbeat cleanly
grooves.description: Two simple snare notes on the final beat make a compact pickup into the next bar.

grooves.name: Fill: Beat Four Sixteenths
grooves.focus: Count four even notes on the last beat
grooves.description: Play four snare notes on beat four. Start slowly and keep all four notes the same distance apart.

grooves.name: Fill: Two-Beat Eighths
grooves.focus: Keep the eighth-note fill even across beats three and four
grooves.description: A short two-beat snare fill that leaves the first half of the measure open for counting.

grooves.name: Fill: Snare to Tom Eighths
grooves.focus: Move from snare to tom without changing the pulse
grooves.description: Play two eighth notes on snare followed by two on tom during the final two beats.

grooves.name: Fill: Eighth-Note Toms
grooves.focus: Keep both hands even while moving around the kit
grooves.description: An easy full-bar tom pattern with one note on every eighth-note count.

grooves.name: Fill: Snare, Toms, Crash
grooves.focus: Shape a short fill and accent its final stroke
grooves.description: Three sixteenths move from snare to tom, with a crash on the last sixteenth as a pickup into the loop.

grooves.name: Fill: Last Two Beats in Sixteenths
grooves.focus: Count e-and-a while moving from snare to tom
grooves.description: An eight-note sixteenth fill across beats three and four, ending with an accented tom pickup.

grooves.name: Fill: Eighth-Note Snare and Tom
grooves.focus: Change drum voices without changing note spacing
grooves.description: Alternate snare and tom on eighth notes for a clear, familiar fill sound.

grooves.name: Fill: Snare-Tom-Snare Eighths
grooves.focus: Make each voice change clear without breaking the pulse
grooves.description: Eighth-note groups move from snare to tom and back to snare, with accents marking the start and finish.

grooves.name: Fill: Beat Four Tom Sixteenths
grooves.focus: Fit four quick notes into beat four without rushing
grooves.description: Move four sixteenths from snare to tom on the final beat, then resolve the phrase on the next downbeat.

grooves.name: Fill: Kick and Snare Eighths
grooves.focus: Keep the feet and hands evenly spaced
grooves.description: Alternate kick and snare for a compact two-beat fill that develops limb coordination.

grooves.name: Fill: Beat Four Triplets
grooves.focus: Fit three even notes across the last beat
grooves.description: A three-note triplet pickup on beat four. Keep the swing subdivision steady through the bar line.

grooves.name: Fill: Snare and Tom Triplets
grooves.focus: Keep all four triplet groups the same width
grooves.description: A full-bar triplet fill that moves between snare and tom with a clear accent on each beat.

grooves.name: Fill: Sixteenth Tom Cascade
grooves.focus: Keep sixteen notes flowing as one phrase
grooves.description: A continuous sixteenth-note run that starts on snare, travels through the tom voice, and finishes with a crash accent.

grooves.name: Fill: Sixteenth Kick, Snare, Tom
grooves.focus: Keep the sixteenth grid steady as the sticking moves around the kit
grooves.description: A full-bar orchestration that threads kick, snare, and tom through an even sixteenth-note stream.

grooves.name: Fill: Linear Kick-Snare-Tom
grooves.focus: Play one voice at a time and preserve the gaps in the phrase
grooves.description: A syncopated linear fill uses kick, snare, and tom without overlapping voices, then resolves on the final crash.

grooves.name: Fill: Sixteenths Accented in Threes
grooves.focus: Keep the pulse steady while accents cross the beat
grooves.description: Sixteenth notes continue evenly as accents repeat every three steps, shifting against the four-beat bar.

grooves.name: Fill: Paradiddle Orchestration
grooves.focus: Accent the paradiddle while moving the notes between snare and tom
grooves.description: An eight-note R-L-R-R, L-R-L-L sticking study orchestrated between snare and tom with accents on each group start.

grooves.name: Fill: Linear Triplet Displacement
grooves.focus: Keep the triplet flow as the kick and hands trade places
grooves.description: A syncopated triplet fill moves a single voice at a time around the kit and accents the final note.

grooves.name: Fill: Six-Eight Compound Tom Run
grooves.focus: Group the six eighth notes in two sets of three
grooves.description: A compound-meter fill places even sixteenths across two dotted-quarter pulses and resolves with a crash.

grooves.name: Fill: Five-Four Sixteenth Cascade
grooves.focus: Count five beats as the fill travels across the longer measure
grooves.description: A five-beat phrase of flowing sixteenths with snare, tom, and kick movement marking the grouping.

grooves.name: Fill: Seven-Eight Grouped Accents
grooves.focus: Feel the 3 + 2 + 2 grouping through the fill
grooves.description: A fourteen-note sixteenth fill in 7/8 marks each group with an accent before resolving at the next bar.

grooves.name: Fill: Sixteenth Tom Build
grooves.focus: Build intensity without changing the sixteenth-note spacing
grooves.description: A dynamic tom build rises through the bar and lands on an accented crash at the end of the phrase.
